question: Fund-count denominator for tail community foundations: for a stratified sample of 60 tail CFs (20 per band $10-50m, $1-10m, <$1m), collect the total number of component funds by type (DAF, designated, field-of-interest, scholarship, agency, unrestricted) from annual reports or audited-statement notes, and add an allocation rule F (opex x DAF funds / all funds) beside rules A and G
conclusion_affected: Per-account DAF cost at tail CFs: rule A gives a median $2,859 and rule G $4,106; a per-fund rule could be higher still, because a DAF is one fund among many and fixed cost per fund is the likely driver
rationale: Rules A and G both scale cost with dollars, so they assume a $40k DAF costs one-sixth of a $240k DAF to run. A fund-count rule is the only way to test a fixed per-fund cost, and the repo holds no non-DAF fund counts

question: Audited functional-expense notes: for the 30 largest tail CFs by DAF assets, find audited financial statements (on the sponsor site or state charity registries that allow public download) whose notes allocate expenses or administrative fees by fund type, and compare the DAF share of cost with rules A and G
conclusion_affected: Which allocation rule (A, G or AM) is closest to how sponsors themselves cost DAFs
rationale: Every DAF cost figure in the tail is an allocation [I]. A sponsor's own fee-income or cost note by fund type is the only primary check on the rule

question: Fee coverage in the tail: once P-B45N33-01 collects published DAF fee schedules for tail sponsors, compute each sponsor's fee revenue at its own schedule and average account, divided by its rule-A and rule-G DAF cost, and count how many tail CFs run DAFs at a loss under each rule
conclusion_affected: Whether tail DAFs are cross-subsidised by unrestricted or endowment income; only 15.3% (A) and 18.0% (G) of tail CFs have allocated cost at or below the 100 bps top-100 census median fee
rationale: The cost side is now computed for 603 tail CFs; the fee side is missing for all 1,240 tail sponsors, so coverage can only be stated against a hypothetical 100 bps

question: Outsourced DAF administration at tail single-issue sponsors: screen Schedule R (related organisations) and Part VII-B for tail single-issue sponsors whose DAFs are administered by a community foundation, a national sponsor or a bank, and re-run the single-issue cost statistics excluding them
conclusion_affected: Single-issue tail cost (median rule A 708 bps, whole-org ceiling 7,174 bps) mixes program operations with DAF admin; some sponsors' DAF cost sits with another entity
rationale: Single-issue sponsors' Part IX is mostly mission delivery (libraries, hospitals, congregations). Two tail single-issue sponsors (Kirkland & Ellis Foundation, Youngstown Area Jewish Foundation) report under 1 bp of DAF assets in operating cost, consistent with administration elsewhere

question: FY2025 completion: re-run scripts/mission_long_tail_cost.py on FY2025 returns once the 144 unmirrored returns reach the GivingTuesday mirror and DAFRC-equivalent corrected FY2025 values exist for the tail
conclusion_affected: Stability of the tail CF median (rule A 211/198/205/184 bps in FY2022-25); FY2025 has only 302-303 tail CF returns
rationale: FY2025 Part IX covers about half the tail, biased to early filers; it is shown only as a robustness row
